headline: South Asia: Security forces thwart terrorists' attempt to infiltrate Pak-Afghan border in Kurram: security sources
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Security forces thwart terrorists' attempt to infiltrate Pak-Afghan border in Kurram: security sources.
- Western Russia: Russian strikes on warehouses in Odesa Oblast cause major fires, killing 1 and injuring 2 – photos.
- Asia: Sri Lanka court convicts 15 over 2019 Easter bombings, 9 acquitted.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Poll: Trump approval falls to record low of 32% as war continues.
- Military Times, 20 hours ago: Poll: Trump approval falls to record low of 32% as war continues.
Only 34% of respondents in a new Reuters/Ipsos poll said they approved of the strikes on Iran.
- Military Times, one hour ago: New Sesame Street programming is a walk in the park for military kids.
Sesame Street has teamed up again with the DoD to continue its programming and resources geared toward military preschool-aged children.
- Military Times, 2 hours ago: US Army awards Lockheed Martin $1.2B PrSM contract.
The U.S. Army awarded Lockheed Martin a PrSM contract worth up to $1.2 billion.
- Military Times, 20 hours ago: Airmen can’t get enough of new, warlike basic training, leaders say.
Six months after the Air Force launched a tougher, more combat-centric training program, airmen and prospective instructors are clamoring to get involved.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Escalating domestic violence impacting St James churches.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 12 hours ago: Escalating domestic violence impacting St James churches.
WESTERN BUREAU: Domestic violence is emerging as an increasingly common issue confronting churches across St James, as pastors are routinely called upon to counsel people struggling with troubled relationships and family conflicts. The Reverend Godfrey Francis, secretary of the St James Ministers Fraternal, said the pressures of modern life, coupled with poor communication and weak conflict resolution skills, were helping to fuel the problem, leaving churches to confront the fallout.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 12 hours ago: ‘I used to say, ‘Good job, police’, but now I feel it’.
Relatives of 35-year-old businessman Jordon Perry Smith took their grief and anger to the streets of Seaford Town, Westmoreland, on Monday, demanding answers over his fatal shooting during a police operation. The protest came three days after Smith was killed at his home in an incident police sources have described as a shoot-out, while his relatives continue to reject that account and accuse members of the Constabulary Force of executing him.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Russia attacks Interpipe facility in Dnipro: four killed, seven injured.
A Russian ballistic missile strike on an Interpipe facility in Dnipro killed four workers, injured seven and forced the plant to suspend operations.
- The Moscow Times, 9 hours ago: One Killed as Ukraine Strikes Refineries in Samara and Bashkortostan.
The Rosneft-operated Kuibyshev refinery in the southern Samara region has been repeatedly targeted throughout the war.
- Ukrainska Pravda, one hour ago: Trump says he could use Graham bill if necessary.
Donald Trump said he could use new powers under the Lindsey Graham sanctions law if necessary, as he called for an end to Russia’s war against Ukraine
Southern Europe - bottom line: Albania to Adopt EU Disability Access Standards – But Will They Be Enforced?.
- Balkan Insight, 11 hours ago: Albania to Adopt EU Disability Access Standards – But Will They Be Enforced?.
Albania is moving to bring its disabled access standards into line with the EU’s own, but activists warn that without funding and effective enforcement, the new law could once again fail to deliver meaningful change.
- Balkan Insight, 11 hours ago: ‘Our War is Being Judged’: In Kosovo, Outrage at Hague Verdict Simmers.
Thousands gather twice a day in Pristina’s main square to protest against last week’s verdict convicting four Kosovo guerrilla leaders of war crimes - and some politicians are demanding legislative action to change the way the Hague court works.

[Leadership] Troops of Sector 2, Joint Task Force North West, Operation FANSAN YAMMA (JTF NW OPFY) have recorded major operational successes in Sokoto State, rescuing 23 kidnapped victims, foiling multiple terrorist attacks and arresting four suspected members of the Lakurawa terrorist group.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 2 hours ago: Nigeria: No, Gunmen Did Not Attack Nigeria's Asaba International Airport - Video Shows Planned Security Simulation.
[Africa Check] IN SHORT: Social media posts claim gunmen attacked Asaba International Airport in Nigeria's Delta state. But the video offered as proof shows a crisis-response simulation organised by security agencies.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Security forces thwart terrorists' attempt to infiltrate Pak-Afghan border in Kurram: security sources.
- Dawn (Pakistan), just now: Security forces thwart terrorists' attempt to infiltrate Pak-Afghan border in Kurram: security sources.
Security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to cross into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Kurram from Afghanistan and also effectively responded to firing by the Afghan Taliban, security sources said on Tuesday. According to the sources, the terrorists tried to infiltrate the border from Nangarhar and Paktia in Afghanistan. They identified the terrorists as those belonging to Fitna-al-Khawarij — a term that the state uses for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 8 hours ago: CDF Munir says armed forces remain resolute in defeating terrorism, ensuring lasting peace: ISPR.
Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir said on Tuesday that the armed forces remained resolute in defeating terrorism and ensuring lasting peace and stability, according to the military’s media wing. Field Marshal Munir made the statement while visiting Peshawar Corps Headquarters, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said. He was received by the Peshawar Corps commander.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: 'Terrific man' Shehbaz gets special mention during Trump's UNGA speech.
United States President Donald Trump on Tuesday called Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif a “terrific man” during his address to the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) as he once again mentioned his role in ending the Pakistan-India conflict in May 2025. During a speech that covered the conflict in Iran, artificial intelligence and criticism of the UN, Trump once again listed conflicts that he had played a role in ending. “Since I took office, it has been my honour to help settle eight wars, and in so doing, become friendly with the leaders of many of those countries,” Trump said.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 3 hours ago: Pakistan, 7 other Muslim nations call upon Israel to fulfil its commitment under Gaza plan.
Pakistan joined other Muslim countries on Tuesday in calling for Israel to “immediately fulfill its outstanding commitments” under the first phase of a plan aimed at ending the conflict in Gaza. The demand was made in a joint statement attributed to the foreign ministers of Pakistan, Egypt, Turkiye, Indonesia, Jordan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates after they met on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
Asia - bottom line: Sri Lanka court convicts 15 over 2019 Easter bombings, 9 acquitted.
- South China Morning Post - China, Al Jazeera - Middle East, Times of India - Top Stories, NDTV - Top Stories, ABC News Australia, one hour ago: Sri Lanka court convicts 15 over 2019 Easter bombings, 9 acquitted.
Sri Lanka’s High Court has found 15 of the 24 men accused of being directly involved in the 2019 Easter Sunday bombings guilty. The attacks killed 279 people and wounded around 500. The three-judge bench found that 14 of the accused were guilty on all charges, which included murder, conspiracy to commit terrorism and possessing firearms and explosives under the Prevention of Terrorism Act. A 15th defendant was found guilty of only some of the charges, while nine others were acquitted. The...

Taiwan’s coastguard fired a supersonic anti-ship missile during a military exercise last week, an unusual move by a civilian law enforcement agency that analysts say could be aimed at complicating potential war plans. The drill matters not only because it highlights the growing integration between the agency and Taiwan’s navy, experts argue, but also because missile-armed coastguard vessels would add another threat the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) would have to account for in a conflict. Russia fired ballistic missiles at the southern Ukrainian industrial cities of Dnipro, Kryvyi Rih and Pavlohrad overnight, killing at least four people and wounding six, the governor of the Dnipropetrovsk region, Oleksandr Hanzha, said on Telegram on Tuesday. The casualties occurred in Dnipro, he said, where people are still believed to be trapped under the rubble of a hit industrial facility. The Russian Defence Ministry confirmed attacks on Ukraine’s metals, chemicals, energy and arms...
- South China Morning Post - China, 2 hours ago: Learning from Ukraine war, Chinese military doctors target injuries from drones.
China’s military medical experts are making progress in finding cures for common injuries seen in drone warfare, drawing on lessons from the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, according to state broadcaster CCTV. Chen Juxiang, a senior Chinese military doctor, told CCTV on Monday that cranio-maxillofacial injuries – damage to the hard and soft tissues of the head – had become a particularly big problem in conflicts dominated by drones. India - bottom line: After Bihar Groping Horror, Shocker From Odisha: Couple Assaulted On Camera.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: After Bihar Groping Horror, Shocker From Odisha: Couple Assaulted On Camera.
The Odisha incident reportedly took place on a road leading towards Kapilash, a popular tourist destination in Dhenkanal district. The couple had travelled to the area on a motorcycle when they were stopped by a group of people.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: China building new next-generation submarine as India's numbers stay constant.
Fresh satellite imagery of China’s Bohai Shipyard shows a submarine believed to be a possible Type 095 nuclear-powered attack submarine under construction. The vessel features an apparent pumpjet propulsion system and X-shaped stern, suggesting efforts to improve stealth, efficiency and manoeuvrability. The development has regional implications as Pakistan expands its submarine fleet with eight Chinese-designed Hangor-class AIP submarines, expected to raise its fleet to 11. India operates 16 conventional and three strategic submarines, but fleet expansion has been delayed.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: 'I'm going to tell the truth': Netanyahu hits back at Mamdani ahead of UN speech.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is set to deliver a significant address at the United Nations General Assembly. In his speech, he intends to staunchly defend military operations conducted by Israel while also targeting New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani. Netanyahu has accused Mamdani of endorsing Hamas and fostering anti-Jewish sentiment, in response to Mamdani's previous remarks labeling him a war criminal responsible for genocide.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Gunmen kill 2 cops during polio vaccination drive in Pakistan's Balochistan.
On Tuesday, gunmen in Balochistan province of Pakistan killed two police officers while they were safeguarding a door-to-door polio vaccination campaign. Thankfully, the health workers giving oral vaccine drops escaped without injury. Sadly, this incident highlights the ongoing security challenges that hamper vaccination drives in Pakistan, leaving it and Afghanistan as the last countries grappling with wild poliovirus transmission.
